subject: English
passage: The Sorrows of Young Werther is a 1774 epistolary novel by Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, translated in 2015 by Sigrid Dubois. Werther, pining for the unattainable Lotte, recognizes the depth of his romantic yearning but holds that it is warranted: ______
prompt: Which quotation from The Sorrows of Young Werther most effectively illustrates the claim?

choices.A: "O ye quiet evenings, ye moonlit paths beneath the lindens, how often have ye witnessed the torrents of my sighs, the fevered pacings of this restless heart, when sleep forsakes me!"
choices.B: "Send her but one glance toward me; for I have no more the power to sustain alone the weight of this longing that bows me to the earth."
choices.C: "I know well my own ardor, it does not escape me; yet, seeing that the cause is of such singular worth, I will never check these wild raptures, so long as breath remains in me."
choices.D: "But never shall I cease from sighs and aching complaint, while I behold the trembling dew upon the meadow, or this golden light of morning."

explanation: Choice C is the best answer. Werther states that he "knows well" his own ardor and that it "does not escape" him, which shows that he is aware of the depth of his romantic yearning. He then adds that "the cause is of such singular worth" — meaning the object of his love merits such feeling — which explicitly frames his yearning as warranted. This quotation therefore satisfies both parts of the claim.
